title: Rust: If/Else Conditionals
description: Use if, else if, and else to make decisions in Rust.

steps.title: Basic If
steps.description: Declare `number = 10`. If it's greater than 5, print `"Greater than 5"`.
hints: The condition must be a bool (no truthy/falsy like JS).
Rust does not require parentheses around conditions.

steps.title: If/Else
steps.description: Declare `age = 16`. If age >= 18 print `"Adult"`, otherwise print `"Minor"`.
hints: The `else` block runs when the if condition is false.
Test with age = 16 to see the else branch.

steps.title: Else If Chain
steps.description: Set `score = 85`. Print `"A"` if >= 90, `"B"` if >= 80, `"C"` if >= 70, else `"F"`.
hints: Use `if score >= 90 { ... } else if score >= 80 { ... } else { ... }`
Conditions are checked in order, first match wins.

verification.failureMessage: Print the correct grade for score = 85.

steps.title: If in a let Statement
steps.description: Declare a variable using if/else as an expression: `let result = if x > 0 { "positive" } else { "non-positive" };` with `x = 7`. Print result.
hints: In Rust, `if` is an expression and can be used on the right side of `let`.
Both arms must return the same type.

verification.failureMessage: Print the result of if expression with x = 7.

steps.title: Nested Conditions
steps.description: Given `x = 15` and `y = 20`, determine if x is even AND y is a multiple of 5. Use nested if statements. Print the result.
hints: Nest the second if inside the first if block.

verification.failureMessage: Print whether x is even and y is a multiple of 5.
